feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: This summer was hot. August shattered global heat records
entry.summary: Scientists say that August was the hottest month ever recorded globally. In the U.S., summer temperatures also shattered heat records.

entry.title: Lawsuit challenges intimidation of DHS observers across the country
entry.summary: The sweeping lawsuit brought by Common Cause argues federal agencies are illegally surveilling and intimidating people who try to peacefully observe federal immigration enforcement activity.

entry.title: How the WNBA became a political prop in the culture wars
entry.summary: Sports journalist Sabreena Merchant says culture war issues related to race and trans athletes threaten to overshadow exceptional play on the WNBA court.

entry.title: Barbara Keating died in the 9/11 attack. She's finally being laid to rest
entry.summary: Barbara Keating died aboard one of the planes that hijackers slammed into the World Trade Center. Her remains were finally identified last year, and her family is gathering for a long-delayed funeral.

entry.title: Trump promises Americans $5K if GOP wins. And, Kirk supporters reflect on his death
entry.summary: President Trump tries to incentivize voters by promising $5,000 to Americans if the GOP wins the midterms. And, young conservatives reflect on the party one year after Charlie Kirk's death.

entry.title: NYC firefighters want answers after release of post-9/11 air quality documents
entry.summary: New York City's firefighters are demanding answers after the city released documents showing how toxic the air quality was following the attacks on the World Trade Center on 9/11.

entry.title: Vance, Trump issue plea for Americans to vote Republican on last night of convention
entry.summary: President Trump again touted his "Trump dividend" in his closing speech at the Republican convention. Vice President Vance used his remarks to urge voters to back Republicans, even if they disagree.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: Trump kicks off Republican midterm convention with primetime speech, Missouri Supreme Court to decide whether to hold secretary of state in contempt, Apple unveils new foldable phone.

entry.title: Maine Gov. Janet Mills on the effect the U.S.-Canada trade war will have on the state
entry.summary: NPR's Michel Martin asks Maine's Democratic Governor Janet Mills about the impact of the escalating U.S.-Canada trade war on her state.

entry.title: Trump officials revive a bid to alter the U.S. census and reshape voting maps
entry.summary: The Trump administration is making a new push to exclude millions of U.S. residents from a key census count that the 14th Amendment says must include the "whole number of persons in each state."
